reason: E1 confirms the baseline premise of poor room-temperature ductility in RHEAs. E2 shows Hf can form strengthening precipitates in HEAs, but it explicitly notes prior work used larger Hf additions (>1 at%) in single-phase FCC alloys, not trace amounts in BCC RHEAs. The specific claims that trace Hf (0.3–0.5 at%) will form nanoscale precipitates in NbMoTaW, that these precipitates will improve ductility via crack deflection, and that the BCC matrix will preserve high-temperature and irradiation properties are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC RHEA with poor room-temperature ductility
Trace Hf addition can promote nanoscale precipitate formation in HEAs
Nanoscale precipitates can improve room-temperature ductility by deflecting cracks and enhancing dislocation mobility
A continuous BCC matrix preserves high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance
Hf is an effective strengthener for B2/intermetallic phases in high-temperature alloys
